description: Remaining Flutter and documentation findings: L-6 (privacy-zone rectangle subtraction overlap) and L-7 (package publish_to none vs README 'ships as MIT package'), plus the spec/doc-drift reconciliation the audit calls out in section 5 (design.md §12 'Known open items: None' is optimistic; reconcile with the deferred adapters and M-3 cross-instance caveat; design §9/§10 vs M-1/M-6). Independent of the backend features; depends on FEAT-004 only to avoid editing README/design concurrently. One atomic user-authored commit per finding/cluster.
steps: COMMIT (L-6): app/lib/vision/privacy_zone_geometry.dart maskBeforeDetection/_subtract subtract each zone from the running region set sequentially; for overlapping zones the strip-splitting decomposition can produce overlapping output rectangles. maskedFraction is already a conservative upper bound (safe direction) and admitDetection (center + threshold) is the real safety gate, and all processing is on-device with no network path. The audit endorses EITHER using a proper rectangle union/subtraction OR documenting the conservative behavior as intentional. Choose: if an exact non-overlapping decomposition is implementable cleanly and keeps all existing privacy_zone tests green, implement it (ensure _subtract across multiple overlapping zones yields non-overlapping output rectangles, e.g. by clipping each produced strip against already-removed zones). Otherwise, make the conservative-overlap behavior explicit: tighten the doc comment on maskBeforeDetection/_subtract to state clearly that output rectangles MAY overlap when input zones overlap, that this only ever makes masking stricter (safe), and that admitDetection (center-in-zone + maskedFraction>=threshold) is the authoritative gate, so overlapping output never relaxes masking. If overlap could ever UNDER-mask (emit a masked pixel), that must be fixed, not just documented — reason about this and state the conclusion. Add/extend a test in app/test/vision/ (find the existing privacy_zone geometry test) covering two OVERLAPPING zones: assert that admitDetection discards a detection whose center is in the overlap and that maskedFraction for the overlap region is clamped to <=1 (never exceeds 1 and never drops below the true covered fraction). Keep analyze clean.

COMMIT (L-7): packages/flutter_ring_captions/pubspec.yaml has publish_to: "none" while README.md frames it as 'ships as a standalone MIT package'. The audit endorses EITHER removing publish_to: none and completing pub.dev metadata if publication is intended, OR clarifying in the README that the package is 'extractable / MIT-licensed' rather than 'published'. Choose the README-clarification path (smallest correct change; actually publishing to pub.dev is out of scope and would need homepage/issue_tracker/topics metadata and a pub.dev account). Update the README.md sentence (around 'ships as a standalone MIT package, flutter_ring_captions') to say the caption/reply logic is extracted into a standalone, MIT-licensed package that is reusable / extractable (not currently published to pub.dev; publish_to is intentionally none). Keep the pubspec publish_to: none and its existing LOW-24 comment. No em/en dashes. No code/test change; this is a docs edit. (If instead publication is clearly intended by the project, the alternative is to remove publish_to and add homepage/issue_tracker/topics — but default to the README clarification and record the choice.)

COMMIT (spec/doc drift, audit section 5): reconcile the specs with reality. In .kiro/specs/threshold-doorbell/design.md §12 'Known open items' (currently 'None as of this revision.'), replace/augment the 'None' with the real deferred items the audit lists so the spec stops claiming no open items: (a) the production device/cloud/Ring adapters are deferred (live WebView session, TTS reply injection, Ring app launch, backend HTTP/WS client, data erasure, re-auth, KMS token store) — they throw/are fixtures today; (b) the Android OAuth deep-link handoff + ProductionAuthPort are deferred so sign-in is not end-to-end on device (H-2); (c) the per-resident ASR cap and single-live-session invariant are enforced per-process only and need a shared store (atomic DynamoDB/Redis counter or lease keyed by residentSub) for the multi-instance topology (M-3). Each with a short date-stamped note consistent with §12's instruction that 'Any new ambiguity must be recorded here'. Also reconcile §9 (route JSON schemas) and §10 (latency metrics) with what FEAT-003 actually did for M-1 and M-6: if FEAT-003 implemented route schemas / wired webhook_ack_ms, note it; if FEAT-003 amended the spec to service-layer validation / app-side metrics, make §9/§10 consistent with that choice. Keep edits factual and dash-free. No test; this is spec text.

After each commit run the relevant gate: for L-6, `export PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH && cd app && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test && dart run tool/lint_ui_copy.dart lib`; for L-7 and the spec/doc commit, no build is needed but run the UI-copy lint if README/lib strings changed and confirm the docs read cleanly. Author every commit as the user (git -c user.name="Suleiman" -c user.email="85356587+suletetes@users.noreply.github.com" commit ...). Stage only the files for that finding.
acceptance_criteria: L-6: privacy_zone_geometry.dart either produces a correct non-overlapping decomposition OR clearly documents the conservative overlap behavior as safe (never under-masks), backed by a test covering two overlapping zones; flutter analyze clean and all app tests pass.

L-7: README.md describes flutter_ring_captions as an extractable / MIT-licensed (not pub.dev-published) package consistent with publish_to: none, or (if publication is intended) publish_to is removed and pub metadata completed; the chosen path is recorded.

spec drift: design.md §12 lists the real deferred items (device/cloud adapters, H-2 deep-link/auth, M-3 cross-instance caps) instead of 'None', and §9/§10 are consistent with how M-1/M-6 were actually resolved in FEAT-003.
flutter analyze --fatal-infos clean, flutter test passing, and the UI-copy dash lint passing after the L-6 commit; docs commits contain no em/en dashes.
Commits are atomic (one finding/cluster each) and authored by Suleiman.
verification: export PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH && cd app && flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test && dart run tool/lint_ui_copy.dart lib
findings:
All three findings addressed in three atomic, Suleiman-authored commits on fix/audit-findings-remediation. Final gate green: flutter analyze --fatal-infos 'No issues found!', flutter test 680 tests 'All tests passed!' (baseline 678 + 2 new overlapping-zone tests), dash lint 'OK, no forbidden dashes in lib'.

L-6 (privacy-zone rectangle subtraction overlap) [documented-as-safe, commit 5fcd588]: Reasoned about whether overlapping zones can under-mask. Conclusion: they cannot. maskBeforeDetection subtracts zones sequentially and each _subtract returns disjoint sub-rectangles that lie entirely OUTSIDE the subtracted zone, so the running region set stays disjoint and zone-free after every step; output rectangles never overlap each other and never overlap a masked zone, even for overlapping input zones (no masked pixel is ever emitted). The only genuine imprecision is in maskedFraction, which sums per-zone intersection areas and double-counts the shared sub-region for overlapping zones, producing a conservative UPPER BOUND clamped to 1. Over-estimating coverage only makes isAdmissibleRegion/admitDetection STRICTER (discards more), so it never relaxes masking and never under-masks. Chosen resolution per briefing (fix only if it could under-mask; it cannot): documented the conservative behavior as intentionally safe. Edits: app/lib/vision/privacy_zone_geometry.dart doc comments on maskedFraction, maskBeforeDetection, and _subtract (LOW-23 references, no logic change). Tests added in app/test/vision/privacy_zone_geometry_test.dart: (1) admitDetection group - two overlapping zones (0.1..0.5 and 0.3..0.7), detection centered in the overlap discarded at default and 0.99 threshold, maskedFraction for the fully-covered overlap region stays within [trueCovered=1.0, 1] and equals 1.0, plus a straddle region asserted >= exact union-covered fraction and <= 1; (2) maskBeforeDetection group - overlapping zones leave no region intersecting any masked zone, output rectangles mutually disjoint, total unmasked area closeTo 0.72 (1.0 - union 0.28). Added a local _unionCoveredFraction test helper for the exact lower bound. analyze clean.

L-7 (publish_to none vs README 'ships as MIT package') [README-clarification, commit 3f07de0]: Chose the README-clarification path (smallest correct change; pub.dev publication out of scope). Edited the root README.md sentence (previously 'ships as a standalone MIT package') to state the caption/reply logic lives in a standalone, MIT-licensed, reusable/extractable package that is NOT currently published to pub.dev (publish_to intentionally none) and is consumed via a git dependency. packages/flutter_ring_captions/pubspec.yaml publish_to: \"none\" and its LOW-24 comment left unchanged. The FEAT-004 Status note was not touched. Docs-only, no code/test. No em/en dashes in the diff.

spec/doc drift (audit section 5) [commit 15c1e34]: Edited .kiro/specs/threshold-doorbell/design.md section 12 'Known open items', replacing 'None as of this revision.' with three dated (2026-10-11) deferred-item notes consistent with section 12's own 'must be recorded here' instruction: (a) production device/cloud/Ring adapters deferred (live WebView session, TTS reply injection, Ring app launch, backend HTTP/WS client, data erasure, re-auth, KMS token store - throw/are fixtures today); (b) Android OAuth deep-link handoff + ProductionAuthPort deferred so sign-in is not end-to-end on device (H-2), accurately noting FEAT-004 added the manifest intent-filter and a tested parser/exchange contract while the live browser+link-listen step and HTTPS exchange transport remain deferred; (c) per-resident ASR cap and single-live-session invariant are per-process only and need a shared store (atomic DynamoDB/Redis counter or lease keyed by residentSub) for the multi-instance topology (M-3). This also resolves the inconsistency where the intro at design.md line 7 already referenced section 12 as non-empty while section 12 still said 'None'. Section 9/section 10 reconciliation: verified FEAT-003 had already amended section 9 (Contract bullet documents service-layer, auth-first validation by choice - the M-1 'amend the spec' path, no per-route Fastify schemas) and section 10 (metrics list includes 'webhook acknowledgement time' and 'schema-validation failure count' - the M-6 server-side wiring). These are mutually consistent and consistent with the new section 12, so no further section 9/10 wording changes were needed (recorded here; no empty commit created). Factual, dash-free.
